topic: A person's invention is already patented by someone else
text: Rain's been hammering down since I left the diner, cold as the truth. Another day, another file I could do without. This one's a corker—a guy comes in, his voice barely above the static, claiming he's cooked up some gadget set to change the world. Got blueprints, he says, the whole shebang. Only problem? Someone else already got their name on it. Patented and signed, he shows me the papers. The lines on his face tell the story better—been at this for months, maybe years. Now, he's asking me to make it right. Like I can wave a magic wand and un-patent something. I got nothing but my wits and a nagging feeling I'm gonna need more than that. Rain's not the only thing that's cold.
